actual_checks: Full exact prompt, wrappers/meta, report/source/author records read; no priors. The literature scope combines complete elementary digit/count deductions with the deep every-pair-of-odd-primes infinitude theorem and precise modern low-multiplicity boundary. Neither 105 infinitude nor 1155 finiteness is claimed.

Legendre floor differences are zero or one and equal floor(2*r_l/p^l). All digits <=(p-1)/2 make every residue <=(p^l-1)/2; any larger digit forces a positive term. The criterion is proved both ways. Exact p^L-interval count includes zero, and the formal generating product is coefficientwise finite. Removing zero subtracts one.

The one-prime count with L=floor(log_p X)+1 gives O_p(X^delta_p), hence either requested set has the p=3 sublinear density-zero bound. This neither proves finiteness nor allows multiplication of independent-base probabilities. B_n is always even for n>=1, so the two-prime theorem must exclude p=2.

Imported two-prime infinitude covers each proper two-factor subproblem, but arbitrary intersections of infinite sets need not be infinite. The modern theorem retains r>=1, epsilon<1/(20r^2) and p_i>=c0(r,epsilon). Fixed positive epsilon allows growing nonzero valuations; varying epsilon changes thresholds/sequences and cannot force zero at fixed primes 3,5,7. Neither theorem supplies a finite cutoff for the four-prime assertion.
